subject: physics_2
question_text: Write a short note on the discovery of neutron?

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked, both equations balanced. ₄Be⁹ + ₂He⁴ → ₆C¹³ + γ: A 9 + 4 = 13, Z 4 + 2 = 6. ₄Be⁹ + ₂He⁴ → ₆C¹² + ₀n¹ + Q: A 13 = 12 + 1, Z 6 = 6 + 0. Chadwick published in 1932; Bothe and Becker reported the penetrating radiation in 1930. The figure carries NO marks because the question does not ask for a labelled diagram.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The arrangement
steps.margin_note: α-particles from the source strike the beryllium target; the radiation that comes out passes through paraffin and knocks protons into the detector.
steps.why: The paraffin is the key part of the picture: it is rich in hydrogen, and protons knocked out of it are what made the invisible radiation measurable.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the paraffin. Without it there are no recoil protons to detect.

recall.must_convey: That the arrangement is drawn: an alpha source, a beryllium target, paraffin, and a detector in a line.
accept: draw the alpha source and beryllium target
reject: beryllium plus helium gives carbon thirteen

steps.memory_tip: Four things in a row: source, beryllium, paraffin, detector.

steps.label: Bothe and Becker
steps.mark_note: Beryllium struck by α-particles gives penetrating radiation
lines: Bothe and Becker found that when beryllium is
bombarded with α-particles of about 5 MeV, a
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the two workers, the target and the penetrating radiation.
steps.why: The radiation passed through several centimetres of lead, far more than any γ ray of that energy should, and that was the first sign that it was not γ radiation at all.
common_mistakes: Saying the beryllium was bombarded with protons. It was α-particles.
Crediting Chadwick with this first step. Bothe and Becker made the observation.

recall.must_convey: That Bothe and Becker bombarded beryllium with alpha particles and obtained a highly penetrating radiation.
accept: Bothe and Becker bombarded beryllium with alpha particles
a highly penetrating radiation was emitted
beryllium plus helium gives carbon thirteen and gamma

steps.memory_tip: Step one is an observation, not a theory: something very penetrating came out of beryllium.

steps.label: The radiation is uncharged
steps.mark_note: Not deflected by electric or magnetic fields
lines: This radiation was not affected by electric
So the particles in it carry no charge.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. No deflection in a field means no charge.
steps.why: A charged particle moving through a magnetic field is always deflected, so a beam that goes straight through both an electric and a magnetic field must be neutral.
common_mistakes: Saying the radiation was γ rays. That was the first guess, and Chadwick showed it was wrong.
Leaving out the fields. The lack of deflection is the evidence.

recall.must_convey: That the radiation was not deflected by electric or magnetic fields, so it is uncharged.
accept: not affected by electric and magnetic fields
reject: mass nearly equal to the proton

steps.memory_tip: Straight through a magnetic field means zero charge.

steps.label: Chadwick's interpretation
steps.mark_note: 1932, a new neutral particle of proton mass
lines: In 1932 James Chadwick let this beryllium
radiation fall on nitrogen and on argon.
From the recoil of those nuclei he showed the
radiation is a stream of new particles with no
charge and mass nearly equal to the proton
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The year 1932, the name Chadwick, and the two facts: no charge, proton mass.
steps.why: A γ ray could not give a nitrogen nucleus the recoil that was measured; only a particle of about the proton mass could, and that measurement is what turned the guess into a discovery.
common_mistakes: Giving the year as 1930 or 1935. Chadwick published in 1932.
Saying the new particle has the same mass as the electron.

recall.must_convey: That in 1932 Chadwick interpreted the beryllium radiation as a new uncharged particle with mass nearly equal to that of the proton.
accept: a new particle with no charge and proton mass

steps.memory_tip: Chadwick 1932: no charge, proton mass, new particle.

steps.label: The reaction and the name
steps.mark_note: The balanced equation and the name neutron
lines: These neutral particles were named neutrons,
written ₀n¹, and the reaction is

lines.text: The neutron ₀n¹ was discovered in 1932.

steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The balanced equation with ₀n¹ on the right.
steps.why: Check both totals: the mass numbers are 9 + 4 = 13 = 12 + 1 and the atomic numbers are 4 + 2 = 6 = 6 + 0, so the equation balances with exactly one neutron.
common_mistakes: Writing ₆C¹³ on the right of this equation. With a neutron emitted the carbon is ₆C¹².
Giving the neutron a charge number other than 0.

recall.must_convey: That the particle was named the neutron, written zero-n-one, and the reaction is beryllium-9 plus helium-4 giving carbon-12 plus a neutron.
accept: beryllium nine plus helium four gives carbon twelve plus a neutron

steps.memory_tip: Same reactants as step one; a neutron out instead of a γ ray, so carbon-13 becomes carbon-12.

insider_note: The four marks follow the story in order: the penetrating radiation, the proof that it is uncharged, Chadwick reading it as a new particle, and the balanced equation.
